00_welcome.mp3: Welcome to Stars Beside You, a planetary twin finder. Before a rover, a solar panel or a lunar base ever reaches the Moon, it can be tested here on Earth, if we find the right place. We compare lunar data from NASA missions with data from all over the Earth, and look for the places that match on what matters most for each mission. There are three missions. Press one for the Rover, where slope and roughness decide everything. Press two for Solar Panels, where sunlight is the key. Press three for the Lunar Base, where temperature and its daily swing matter most.
m1_rover.mp3: Rover. A rover's journey depends on the ground beneath its wheels, so we match places by slope and surface roughness. On the Moon, we search near the south pole, where NASA plans to look for water ice. All five analogs share the same lunar twin: a gentle plain at 76.5 degrees south, about 160 kilometers from Casatus crater. Here are the five best analogs on Earth. m3_base.mp3: Lunar Base. A base has to survive the cold, and the swing between day and night, so we match places by temperature and daily temperature range.
